input.question: Why is it that when I'm really drunk I can barely taste what I'm drinking, but I feel like I'm hypersensitive to how food tastes?
input.ground_truth: Because you are becoming taste blind to the beer over time. If you sit in a room that has a nice smell you'll eventually not be able to smell it over time. Same thing applies if you drink Keystone all night (the fact that it has a mild taste and makes you intoxicated only amplifies the effect) but if you eat something that is very flavorful then it makes a greater impression.

Question: Why is it that when I'm really drunk I can barely taste what I'm drinking, but I feel like I'm hypersensitive to how food tastes?

response.prediction:
Okay! Imagine you have a magic blanket that covers your tongue when you drink a lot of something with alcohol, like juice with a lot of medicine in it. That blanket makes it hard for you to taste the drink. So when you’re really drunk, your tongue can’t feel the drink very well, and it doesn’t taste as strong or interesting.

But when you eat food, that magic blanket isn’t as strong on your tongue. So the food feels super strong and exciting—like everything tastes extra yummy or spicy or tasty! That’s why you might feel like food tastes way better or stronger when you’re really drunk, even though drinks don’t taste as good.
